content.title: How UCLA knocked off Texas to reach women's NCAA Tournament championship game
content.text: UCLA takes down TexasUCLA is headed to the national championship game for the first time in program history after beating Texas 51-44 in the women’s NCAA Tournament Final Four.The Bruins will face another SEC program, South Carolina, on Sunday for the title. UCLA center Lauren Betts had 16 points, 11 rebounds and three blocked shots, including a huge block on Madison Booker late in the game with the Bruins leading by three points.Share your thoughts on the game: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementVic Schaefer applauds Harmon as she comes off the court and is giving her a long talk now. They both smile at each other and exchange a long hug before shaking hands with UCLA.A sad goodbye for HarmonYou can start to see the emotions on Rori Harmon's face as she processes the end of her college career. Tough way to go out, even if Texas bettered its performance from last year's Final Four.Q4 3.1 – UCLA 49, Texas 44Oh no.What a disastrous possession for Texas. Madison Booker slips while driving to the basket, and Kyla Oldacre misses a baseline jumper that ricochets off the backboard.Rice hits clutch free throws Getty ImagesQ4 0:13 – UCLA 49, Texas 44Kiki Rice makes both of her free-throw attempts to boost the UCLA lead up to two possessions. 13 seconds left, and Texas is running out of time.Q4 0:14 – UCLA 47, Texas 44After a quick Texas foul on the inbounds play, Texas coach Vic Schaefer calls a timeout to coordinate the Longhorns’ defense. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementOne job for UCLA: Do not turn the ball over.Feels like the obvious, but after UConn-Duke on the men's side, we know it’s not always.UCLA calls its final timeout Getty ImagesLast timeout for UCLA, which has had to use three in the last 10 minutes to avoid five-second inbounding violations.HUGE block from Lauren Betts.UCLA being smart here to not shoot the ball. Hold on to it.Betts with the block! Imagn ImagesQ4 0:18 – UCLA 47, Texas 44Madison Booker takes a defensive rebound coast to coast but is denied on her reverse layup attempt by, who else, Lauren Betts. What a swat by Betts!We're 18 seconds away from the end of regulation, and UCLA has just used its last timeout.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementRori Harmon picks off Kiki Rice’s dribble and it leads to a Jordan Lee bucket. Longhorns are making things happen after being down 13.UCLA lead down to 3 points Getty ImagesQ4 0:55 – UCLA 47, Texas 44Texas has cut its deficit to three points!!Jordan Lee spins in the post and banks in the layup to cut the UCLA lead to 47-44. UCLA calls timeout after surrendering seven straight points.It seemed like the UCLA bench was up in arms because Dugalic went too early, but you could clearly hear Cori Close yell "that's a f***in foul" when the play ended.The broadcast just showed some impressive Lauren Betts numbers: in her time at UCLA, she’s averaging 17 ppg, shooting 61 percent. But in the NCAA Tournament, she averages 22 on 68 percent. Made for the moment, if you will.Betts' double-double powers UCLA to late advantage Getty ImagesQ4 2:18 – UCLA 47, Texas 40Lauren Betts beats an expiring clock and nails a post shot to interrupt the Texas run. Betts is shining on the Final Four stage: 16 points on efficient 7-10 shooting, 10 rebounds and two blocks. And while less quantifiable, her defense on Madison Booker has swung this game and disrupted the Texas offense.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUCLA has moved past the tying shoes to waste time tactic, instead Kneepkens just walked off the court painfully slowly before the bench signaled for an appeal.Cori Close is not happy with that call on Dugalic. "NO WAY" she screams. "NO WAY."Betts-Kneepkens connection culminates in another 3-pointerUCLA loves the inside out. Lauren Betts to Gianna Kneepkens and UCLA takes its largest lead of the night, up 45-32 with four minutes on the clockTexas cuts into UCLA's leadQ4 3:35 – UCLA 45, Texas 37We still have 3:39 to go in the fourth quarter, but it’s already the most high-scoring quarter of the game. It's not a high bar.Jordan Lee and Madison Booker are knocking down shots for the Longhorns, who trim a UCLA lead that reached a game-high 13 points down to eight.
